title: Türkic Seals & Clan Marks: Proto-Writing or Identity Markers?
research_question: Were Turkic clan seals and identity marks (damgalar) precursors to or parallel developments with Old Turkic runic writing?
sub_questions: What was the chronological relationship between seal/mark usage and runic writing emergence?
Were damgalar used as identity markers, property marks, or proto-writing symbols?
Is there archaeological or textual evidence of evolution from seals to runes?
How did damgalar vary regionally (Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar, other Turkic groups)?
What role did totemism and clan structure play in damgalar design?

story_candidates.title: The Missing Link: From Seal to Script
story_candidates.core_tension: Historians debate whether Turkic seals were proto-writing or merely identity markers—new archaeological evidence may settle this.

story_candidates.title: Totem & Trade: The Social Life of Damgalar
story_candidates.core_tension: Damgalar served multiple functions (identity, property, spiritual) that conventional writing systems didn't—revealing a complex pre-literate society.

scope_note: Item range 201-240 (40 items); focus on primary evidence (seals, inscriptions, archaeological context), secondary scholarship (Turkish, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Russian), and historiographical debates.
research_depth_level: Academic + Archival (claim-dependent), due to contested historiography and limited Western scholarship
